name: Tex-Mex Beef and Rice Skillet Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2 cans (780 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2 cans (375 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 1 bag (168 g)
Chili Powder: 2 tsp ground chipotle (or chili powder) (16 g)
steps: Brown the ground beef in a large skillet and drain the grease.
Stir in the paprika and cumin and cook a minute to wake up the spices.
Add the diced tomatoes, black beans, and corn and let it all simmer together.
Fold in the cooked rice and stir until it is heated through and coated.
Top with shredded cheddar and let it melt before you dish it into bowls.

name: Thai Basil Beef Bowls with Coconut Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Make the coconut rice: combine the rice, coconut milk, and enough water to hit your usual rice liquid ratio, add a pinch of salt, and cook covered on low until tender. Fluff and set aside.
Shred the carrots, slice the jalapeno and red bell pepper, and chop the green onions.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over high heat and brown the ground beef hard, breaking it up and letting it crisp. Add the garlic and jalapeno for the last 2 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce, lime juice, brown sugar, and a pinch of cayenne. Let it bubble until the liquid reduces to a glaze that coats the beef.
Turn off the heat and fold in the fresh basil and bell pepper so they stay bright.
Build bowls: coconut rice on the bottom, basil beef on top, shredded carrots and green onions to finish.

name: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Krapow)
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3.5 lb (1575 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 4.75 tbsp (84 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce and sugar together in a small bowl with a splash of water. Have it standing by, because once this cooks there is no time to measure anything.
Chop the chicken thighs into small pieces, roughly the size of a thumbnail, so they cook through in the time a stir fry allows.
Cook the rice first and let it steam covered off the heat while you do everything else.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok over the highest heat you have. Add the minced garlic and sliced jalapeno and cook 20 seconds, just until the garlic turns pale gold.
Add the chicken in batches so the pan never cools down and stir hard for 4 to 5 minutes until it is cooked through and browned in spots. Crowding the pan is the one mistake that ruins this dish.
Return all the chicken to the pan, pour in the sauce, and let it bubble and reduce for a minute until it clings to the meat.
Kill the heat, throw in the fresh basil and the sliced green onions all at once, and fold until the basil just wilts. Then combine with the rice in your mixing pot.

name: Thai Basil Pork Pad Kra Pao Bowls
ingredients: Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 1 cups (252 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mince the garlic and jalapenos together, coarsely, so you get bursts of heat rather than an even burn.
Stir the fish sauce, soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, and chicken broth together in a bowl so the sauce goes in all at once later.
Heat the vegetable oil in a very large skillet or wok over high heat until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and jalapenos and cook for about thirty seconds, just until fragrant, without letting the garlic brown.
Add the ground pork and cook hard, breaking it up, until it is browned and the liquid has cooked off.
Pour in the sauce mixture and let it bubble and glaze the pork, then season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Kill the heat, dump in all the basil at once, and fold it through until it just wilts.

name: Thai Cashew Chicken
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1323 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Toast the cashews in a dry skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pan, until they smell nutty and go a shade darker. Tip them onto a plate immediately so they stop cooking.
Whisk the soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together with a splash of water and set the sauce next to the stove.
Cook the rice first and let it steam covered off the heat while you stir fry.

Slice the chicken breast thin. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok over high heat and sear the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until browned and cooked through, then set it aside.
Add the minced garlic to the hot pan for 15 seconds, then the sliced onion, red bell pepper and green bell pepper. Stir fry 2 to 3 minutes so they soften at the edges but keep their bite.
Return the chicken, pour in the sauce, and toss for a minute until everything is coated and the liquid has reduced to a glaze.
Kill the heat and fold in the toasted cashews and the green onions, then combine with the rice in your mixing pot.

name: Thai Coconut Curry Turkey Meatballs
ingredients: Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 7 tbsp (105 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.

Mix the ground turkey with the bread crumbs, eggs, garlic powder, ground ginger, dried basil, salt, and black pepper. Do not overwork it, mix just until it holds. Roll into meatballs about the size of a golf ball, roughly 3 per serving.
Brown the meatballs in the vegetable oil in batches over medium-high heat. They do not need to cook through yet, just get color.
In the same pot, cook the onion until soft, then add the garlic, fresh ginger, and red curry paste and fry 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and stir until the paste dissolves into a smooth, creamy curry sauce.
Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer in the coconut curry until they hit 165F in the center, about 10 to 12 minutes.
Finish with the lime juice and fresh basil, then serve the meatballs and sauce over the rice.

name: Thai Drunken Noodles with Chicken (Pad Kee Mao)
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 46 oz dry (1303 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 2.75 lb (1191 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 1 cups (252 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dry rice noodles in warm water until they are pliable but still firm in the center, about 20 minutes. They finish cooking in the pan, so pulling them early is correct.
Whisk the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce and sugar together with a splash of water. Have it ready at the stove; there is no time to mix once the pan is hot.
Slice the chicken thighs thin. Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok as hot as it goes and sear the chicken in batches for 3 to 4 minutes until browned, then set it aside.
Add the minced garlic, sliced jalapeno and sliced onion to the same pan and cook 1 minute until fragrant and just starting to soften.

Add the drained noodles and the sauce and toss constantly for 3 to 4 minutes. Let the noodles sit still for a few seconds at a time so they char in spots, then move them again. Those charred edges are the whole point of the dish.
Return the chicken and toss everything together until the sauce has coated every strand and there is no liquid pooling in the pan.
Kill the heat and fold in the fresh basil and green onions so they wilt from the residual heat instead of cooking down to nothing.

name: Thai Green Curry Chicken
ingredients: Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 10 oz (280 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2380 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Open the coconut milk cans without shaking them and spoon the thick cream off the top into your largest pot. Reserve the thin liquid underneath.
Heat the pot over medium-high and cook that coconut cream with the vegetable oil for 3 to 5 minutes until it splits and you can see clear oil pooling.

Add the curry paste, minced garlic, grated ginger and lemongrass paste and fry them in that oil for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens and smells sharp and fragrant. This is the step people skip and it is the one that matters.
Add the chicken thighs cut into strips and turn them in the paste for 3 minutes, then pour in the reserved coconut liquid and the chicken broth.
Add the cubed eggplant and simmer uncovered 15 to 20 minutes until the eggplant is soft and the sauce has reduced and thickened.
Season with the fish sauce, sugar, salt and black pepper, then add the snow peas and cook 2 minutes so they stay bright and snappy.
Kill the heat and stir in the lime juice, the fresh basil and the thin-sliced onion. Cook the rice separately and fold it in, or hold it in the containers underneath.

name: Thai Peanut Pork Tenderloin Rice Bowl
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package. While it is hot, stir in half the lime juice and the fresh cilantro. Cover and set aside.
Cut the pork tenderloin into medallions about an inch thick and season with salt, black pepper, and ground coriander.
Sear the medallions in olive oil over medium-high heat, about 3 to 4 minutes per side, until they hit 145F. Rest them on a plate.

In the same pan, add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, then pour in the coconut milk and whisk in the peanut butter and brown sugar. Simmer until it thickens into a smooth peanut sauce, then finish with the rest of the lime juice.
Stir the spinach into the warm peanut sauce until wilted through.
Build bowls: lime rice down, sliced pork on top, peanut sauce spooned over everything.

name: Thai Pork Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao)
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 42 oz dry (1191 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak or boil the rice noodles per the package until just shy of tender, then drain and rinse. They finish in the pan.
Stir together the fish sauce, soy sauce, and rice vinegar for the sauce.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or pot over high heat. Cook the onion 2 minutes, then add the garlic and jalapeno for 1 minute more.
Add the ground pork and brown it hard, breaking it into crumbles, until cooked through with crispy edges.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss until the noodles soak it up and everything is coated.
Kill the heat and fold in the fresh basil, sliced bell pepper, and lime juice. The basil should wilt in the residual heat, not cook.

name: Thai Red Curry Chicken Rice Bowls
ingredients: Red Curry Paste (Thai Kitchen): 7 tbsp (105 g)
Boneless Skinless Chicken Breast (Member's Mark): 5.25 lb (2381 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Cut the chicken breast into bite-size pieces and season with salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high and brown the chicken in batches until cooked to 165F, then remove.
In the same pot, cook the green onions, garlic, and jalapeno for 2 minutes, then add the red curry paste and fry it 1 to 2 minutes until it darkens and smells intense.
Pour in the coconut milk, stir in the fish sauce and brown sugar, and simmer about 5 minutes until the curry is smooth and lightly thickened.
Return the chicken, simmer another minute or two to coat, then finish with the lime juice and cilantro.
Serve the coconut curry chicken over the rice.

name: Thai Turkey Larb Bowls
ingredients: Jalapeno: 3-4 dry chiles or 1.5 Tbsp chile powder (35 g)
Fresh Cilantro: 1/2 cup rough chopped (30 g)
steps: Heat a little olive oil in a large skillet and brown the ground turkey.
Add the chopped onion and green peppers and cook until they soften.
Stir in the lime juice and honey to build that classic sweet-and-sour larb balance.
Let it simmer a couple minutes so the flavors soak in, then season with salt to taste.
Serve it over cooked white rice with extra lime on the side.

name: Trinidad Chicken Pelau
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 3 lb (1323 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the chicken thighs with the cajun seasoning, minced garlic, grated ginger, dried thyme, black pepper, salt and most of the chopped cilantro. Let it marinate at least an hour, or overnight.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear and set it aside to drain.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest heavy pot over medium-high, add the brown sugar, and let it melt and bubble until it goes dark amber and starts to smoke slightly. This is the burnt sugar step and it is what makes pelau pelau, so stay at the stove.
Add the marinated chicken all at once and stir hard so every piece takes the caramel. Cook 5 to 7 minutes until browned, then add the diced onion, minced jalapeno, ketchup and bay leaves.
Stir in the drained rice, pigeon peas and cubed sweet potato and coat everything in the caramel.
Pour in the coconut milk and chicken broth, season with the paprika and more salt, and bring to a boil. Drop to the lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 25 to 30 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest it covered off the heat 10 minutes, pull the bay leaves, and fold from the bottom with the remaining cilantro so the browned rice at the base gets spread through.

name: Trinidadian Curry Chicken Bowls
ingredients: Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh (Member's Mark): 8.5 lb (3810 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Blend or finely chop the cilantro, garlic, jalapeno, and half the onion into a rough green seasoning paste. Toss the chicken thighs, cut into large chunks, with the paste and a big pinch of salt. Let it sit at least 15 minutes, longer if you have it.
Stir the curry powder, turmeric, cumin, and garam masala with a few tablespoons of water to make a slurry.

Heat the vegetable oil in your largest pot over medium-high. Pour in the curry slurry and fry it, stirring, until the water cooks off and the oil separates and the kitchen smells serious, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the chicken and remaining onion and stir to coat every piece in the fried curry. Cook 5 minutes, letting the chicken release its own liquid.
Add the potatoes, peeled and cut in chunks, plus enough water to come halfway up. Cover and simmer until the potatoes are tender, the gravy thickens, and the chicken reads 165F, about 25 minutes.
Taste for salt and black pepper, and mash a few potato chunks against the pot wall if you want the gravy thicker.

name: Tunisian Harissa Coconut Beef Meatballs
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Grate or very finely chop about a third of the onion and mix it into the ground beef with half the garlic, a good handful of chopped cilantro, the garam masala, salt, and pepper.
Roll the mixture into meatballs of a consistent size. Uniform meatballs cook evenly and portion evenly, which matters more here than looks.
Sear the meatballs in the vegetable oil in batches, turning to brown them on several sides. They do not need to cook through yet.
Chop the remaining onion and cook it in the same pot until soft, then add the rest of the garlic for a minute.
Stir in the harissa paste and let it fry for a minute, then pour in the coconut milk and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Return the meatballs, cover, and simmer 20 to 25 minutes until they are cooked through and the sauce has thickened around them.
Cook the rice separately and scatter the remaining cilantro over the top before portioning.

name: Turkey a la King over Egg Noodles
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 30.75 oz dry (875 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter in your largest pot over medium heat and cook the sliced mushrooms and diced onion for 10 to 12 minutes, until all the mushroom liquid has cooked away and they start to brown.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir constantly for two full minutes. This is a big roux and it needs the time to lose its raw taste.
Pour in the chicken broth gradually, whisking hard after each addition so no lumps form, and bring it to a simmer until it thickens.
Stir in the heavy cream and season with the garlic powder, salt, and plenty of black pepper, then let it bubble gently for 5 minutes.
Fold in the diced turkey breast and warm it through without boiling, since hard boiling will make the turkey tighten and go stringy.
Add the frozen peas and the sliced olives at the very end and let the residual heat warm them for 3 to 4 minutes, which keeps the peas bright instead of gray.
Cook egg noodles separately and spoon the a la king over them just before portioning, so the noodles do not swell and drink the sauce overnight.

name: Turkey Albondigas Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Mix the ground turkey with the eggs, bread crumbs, uncooked rice, minced garlic, dried oregano, ground cumin, salt and black pepper, then roll it into meatballs about the size of a golf ball.
Brown the meatballs on a sheet pan in a hot oven, around 400F for 15 minutes, so they hold together when they hit the broth.
Heat the vegetable oil in your big pot and cook the diced onion until soft, then add the carrots and celery and give them a few minutes.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and the chicken broth, bring to a simmer, and add the cubed potatoes.
Slide the meatballs in gently and simmer 20 minutes, until the rice inside them has swelled and the potatoes are tender.
Add the chopped zucchini and simmer just 5 more minutes so it stays firm, then stir in the chopped cilantro off the heat.

name: Turkey Alfredo Rotini Bake
ingredients: Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 18.5 oz (527 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the rotini about 2 minutes short of the box time and drain it. It will finish cooking in the sauce in the oven, and pasta cooked twice to full is mush.

Slice the mushrooms and cook them in a dry hot pan until they give up their water and it evaporates, about 8 minutes. Dry pan first, then season. That is how you get browned mushrooms instead of gray ones.
Add the ground turkey to the pan and brown it, breaking it up, with salt and black pepper, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Stir in the alfredo sauce and a splash of water, and let it warm through until it loosens into a pourable sauce.
Fold the drained pasta into the sauce so every piece is coated, then spread it into your baking pans.
Cover with the mozzarella and bake at 375F for 25 minutes, until it bubbles around the edges and the cheese has browned in patches.
Let it rest 10 minutes, then transfer it into your weighed pot for portioning.

name: Turkey and Stuffing Casserole
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 5.5 oz (158 g)
Stuffing Mix (Kraft Stove Top (USDA SR)): 15 cups (830 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat, sprinkle in the flour, and whisk for two minutes until it smells nutty instead of raw.
Pour in the chicken broth and the milk slowly, whisking the whole time, and cook until the gravy thickens enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Season the gravy with the onion powder, garlic powder, poultry seasoning, salt, black pepper, and a few dashes of hot sauce, then take it off the heat.
Stir in the Greek yogurt and the shredded cheddar off the heat so the yogurt does not break, then fold in the diced turkey breast and the frozen peas.
Spread the filling into a greased 9x13 pan and level it out.
Prepare the stuffing mix per the box directions but hold back a little of the liquid, then spoon it over the filling in an even layer and press it down lightly.
Bake at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes, uncovered, until the stuffing is browned on top and the gravy bubbles at the edges. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Ants Climbing a Tree (Glass Noodles)
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 43.5 oz dry (1233 g)
Doubanjiang (Lee Kum Kee (Chili Bean Sauce Toban Djan)): 4 oz (112 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak the dried noodles in warm water until they are pliable but still firm, about 15 minutes, then drain them. They finish cooking in the braise, so undercook them now on purpose.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or wide pot, add the grated ginger and the white parts of the green onions, and cook 30 seconds.
Add the ground turkey and brown it into fine crumbles until it is cooked through to 165F.

Push the meat aside and fry the doubanjiang in the oil for 1 minute until it turns the fat a deep red. This step is what pulls the flavor out of the paste, and skipping it leaves the dish tasting flat and raw.
Add the chicken broth, soy sauce, and sugar, stir everything together, and bring it to a simmer.
Add the drained noodles, stir to submerge them, and simmer 6 to 8 minutes until they have drunk up most of the liquid and gone glossy. Stir often so they do not weld to the bottom.
Kill the heat, fold in the green onion tops, and move everything into your weighed pot.

name: Turkey Biscuit Pot Pie Casserole
ingredients: Cream of Mushroom Soup (Campbell's (USDA SR)): 1.8 cans (522 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Whisk the flour into about a cup of the cold milk in a jar until there are no lumps. Doing this cold is the whole trick to a smooth filling.
Warm the rest of the milk with the condensed cream of mushroom soup in a large pot over medium heat, stirring until it is smooth.
Pour in the flour slurry and cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until the sauce thickens to gravy. Season with salt and plenty of black pepper.
Fold in the diced turkey breast and the frozen peas, then pour the filling into a greased 9x13 pan. It should be hot going into the oven so the biscuits cook through from below.
Open the biscuit cans and cut each biscuit in half, then arrange the halves cut side down across the top of the filling in even rows.
Bake at 375F for 30 to 35 minutes, until the biscuits are deep golden on top and cooked through underneath. If they brown too fast, tent the pan with foil.
Rest 10 minutes before portioning so the filling sets under the biscuits instead of running.

name: Turkey Cabbage Roll Soup
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered.
Brown the ground turkey in olive oil in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until it is cooked through.
Add the diced onion, celery and carrots and cook until they start to soften, then stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Core and chop the cabbage into ribbons and pile it into the pot. It will look like too much. Give it five minutes and it will not be.
Pour in the diced tomatoes with their juice and the chicken broth, add the dried oregano, Italian seasoning and dried thyme, and bring it to a simmer.
Simmer 25 to 30 minutes until the cabbage is fully tender, then season with salt and black pepper and stir in the chopped fresh basil off the heat.

name: Turkey Cajun Dirty Rice Skillet
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (168 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in your largest heavy pot over medium heat until crisp, then leave the fat in the pot. That fat is the foundation.
Rinse and trim the chicken livers, pat them dry, and cook them hard in the bacon fat for 4 to 5 minutes until browned outside and barely pink inside. Pull them out and chop them fine.
Add the ground turkey to the pot and brown it well, letting it stick and scrape up off the bottom. The browned bits on the pan are what make the rice dirty.
Stir in the diced onion, green bell pepper, and celery and cook 6 to 8 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, Cajun seasoning, dried thyme, salt, and black pepper.
Return the chopped livers and bacon to the pot, add the dry rice, and stir for two minutes so every grain gets coated in the fat and seasoning.
Pour in the chicken broth, drop in the bay leaves, bring it to a boil, then cover and simmer on low for 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Kill the heat and let it sit covered another 10 minutes, then pull the bay leaves, fluff with a fork, and fold in the sliced green onions.

name: Turkey Chapli Kebab Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Drain the diced tomatoes well and chop them fine. Wet tomato makes patties that fall apart, so squeeze the liquid out before it goes anywhere near the meat.
Mix the ground turkey with the drained tomato, minced garlic, grated ginger, chopped jalapeno, chopped cilantro, eggs, flour, cumin, coriander, garam masala, salt, and black pepper.
Chill the mixture 20 minutes in the fridge. Cold mix holds its shape and this is the difference between kebabs and a sheet pan of crumbles.
Form flat patties, about half an inch thick and wider than you think, and lay them on sheet pans brushed with the melted butter.
Bake at 425F for 15 minutes, then run them under the broiler 3 to 4 minutes until the tops char in spots and the meat reaches 165F.
Squeeze the lime juice over the hot patties and scatter the thinly sliced onion on top so it softens in the residual heat.
Cook the rice and move it into your weighed pot while the kebabs rest.

name: Turkey Chile Relleno Casserole Skillet
ingredients: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 34.5 oz (980 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Halve and seed the green bell peppers, lay them cut side down on a sheet pan, and broil 8 to 10 minutes until the skins blister and blacken in patches.
Cover the hot peppers with foil for 10 minutes to steam, then slip off the loose skins and cut them into wide strips. That char is the flavor of the whole dish.
Brown the ground turkey in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high, then add the diced onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, salt, and black pepper and cook one minute, then sprinkle the flour over everything and stir for two minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer 5 minutes until the sauce thickens and coats the meat rather than pooling around it.
Fold in the charred pepper strips and about half the Mexican cheese blend, then spread the mixture level in the skillet.
Cover with the remaining cheese and bake at 375F for 20 minutes, then broil 2 to 3 minutes until the top browns and blisters. Rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: High-Protein Turkey Chili Mac
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 2 cans (600 g)
Fat Free Cheddar (Great Value): 1 bag (180 g)
Chicken Broth (Swanson): 2 1/2 cups low sodium (1800 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 6.6 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with the chopped onion in a large skillet.
Boil the penne pasta separately until just shy of tender, then drain.
Stir the black beans, diced tomatoes, and tomato paste into the turkey and let it simmer.
Fold in the cooked pasta so every noodle catches the chili.
Melt the fat-free cheddar over the top and stir it through before you portion it out.

name: Turkey Chili Verde with White Beans
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice separately per the package and set it aside covered.
Brown the ground turkey in the olive oil in your big pot over medium-high heat, breaking it up until it is cooked through.
Add the diced onion and cook until translucent, then stir in the minced garlic for the last minute.
Pour in the jarred salsa verde and the chicken broth, scrape the bottom of the pot, and bring it to a simmer.
Add the drained cannellini beans, mash a scoop of them against the side of the pot to thicken the chili, and simmer 25 minutes.
Season with salt and black pepper, stir in the chopped cilantro off the heat, and keep the sour cream separate for topping.

name: Turkey Cordon Bleu Casserole
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice and spread it across the bottom of a greased 9x13 pan as the base layer.
Melt most of the butter in a large pot over medium heat, add the garlic for one minute, then whisk in the flour and cook two minutes until it stops smelling raw.
Pour in the milk slowly while whisking and cook until the sauce thickens, then season with the Dijon mustard, garlic powder, salt, black pepper, and a small pinch of nutmeg.
Take the pot off the heat and melt in the shredded Swiss cheese, stirring until the sauce is smooth. Swiss will turn stringy over direct heat, so patience here pays.
Fold the diced turkey breast and the diced ham into the sauce, then pour it over the rice and spread it level.
Toss the bread crumbs with the remaining melted butter until they look like wet sand, then scatter them across the top in an even layer.
Bake at 350F for 30 to 35 minutes until the crumbs are golden and the edges bubble, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Corn Chowder
ingredients: Hickory Smoked Bacon (Great Value): 0.25 lb (146 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 2.3 cans (1001 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Chop the bacon and render it in your big pot with the olive oil until crisp. Lift the bacon out and leave the fat.
Add the butter, then the diced onion and celery, and cook until soft. Stir in the garlic for the last minute.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir for two minutes so it loses the raw taste and coats everything.
Pour in the chicken broth while stirring, add the peeled and cubed potatoes, and simmer until the potatoes are fork tender and starting to break down.
Add the drained corn and the cooked turkey breast and bring it back to a simmer.
Stir in the heavy cream and the hot sauce, warm it through without boiling, then season with salt and black pepper and scatter the reserved bacon back on top.

name: Turkey Divan Broccoli Rice Bake
ingredients: Cream of Chicken Soup (generic condensed (USDA)): 3.5 cans (1043 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 14 oz (396 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice and let it cool slightly. It goes into the pan already cooked, since it will not soften properly in a thick cream sauce.
Cut the turkey breast into bite-size pieces, season with salt and black pepper, and cook them through in a skillet to 165F, or use turkey you already roasted.
Whisk the cream of chicken soup, heavy cream, mayonnaise, curry powder, garlic powder, onion powder, and black pepper together into a smooth sauce.
Steam or thaw the broccoli florets just until bright green and still firm. Overcooked broccoli in a casserole goes gray and sulfurous, and there is no coming back from that.
Fold the rice, turkey, broccoli, sliced olives, most of the green onions, and about two thirds of the cheddar into the sauce, then spread it in your baking pans.
Toss the bread crumbs with the melted butter and the rest of the cheddar, and scatter that over the top.
Bake at 350F for 30 minutes until the edges bubble and the crumbs turn deep golden, then rest 10 minutes before you touch it.

name: Turkey Drunken Noodles (Pad Kee Mao)
ingredients: Rice Noodles (Thai Kitchen): 45.5 oz dry (1293 g)
Oyster Sauce (Lee Kum Kee): 6.75 oz (189 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Soak or boil the rice noodles per the package until just shy of tender, drain, and rinse.
Stir together the soy sauce, oyster sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar, and sriracha for the sauce.
Heat your largest skillet or pot over high heat and brown the ground turkey, breaking it into crumbles, until cooked through to 165F with some crispy edges.
Add the garlic and jalapeno and stir fry 1 minute.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss until the noodles drink up the sauce and everything is glossy.
Off the heat, fold in the green onions and fresh basil so they wilt without cooking flat.

name: Turkey Egg Roll in a Bowl over Rice
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Shred the cabbage thin and slice the onion. Do this before you turn the stove on, because once the pan is hot this dish moves fast.
Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, and brown sugar together in a small bowl so the sauce is ready to pour.
Heat the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or a wide pot over medium-high, add the ground turkey, and brown it hard, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F.
Add the sliced onion and the minced garlic and cook 3 minutes until fragrant.
Pile in the cabbage. It will look like too much and then it will cook down by half in about 6 minutes. Stir it often and stop while it still has some bite left.
Pour in the sauce, toss everything to coat, and cook 2 minutes more so the liquid clings instead of pooling in the bottom.
Cook the rice, move it into your weighed pot, and slice the green onions for the top.

name: Ground Turkey Fajita Rice Bowls
ingredients: 1/3 Fat Cream Cheese (Great Value): 1 block (65 g)
Garlic: 2 frozen garlic cubes or minced cloves (28 g)
steps: Brown 6.1 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with the sliced onions and green bell peppers.
Cook the rice separately so it stays fluffy and portions clean.
Stir in the tomato paste, salsa verde, and cream cheese until the turkey turns saucy and coats everything.
Let it simmer a few minutes so the flavors pull together.
Spoon the fajita turkey over the rice in each container.

name: Turkey Florentine Rice Bake
ingredients: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 9.25 oz (264 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice and spread it across the bottom of a greased 9x13 pan as the base layer.
Thaw the frozen chopped spinach and squeeze it dry in a clean kitchen towel, wringing hard. You want a compact ball, not a wet clump.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat, add the diced onion and sliced mushrooms, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the mushroom liquid cooks away.
Whisk in the flour and cook two minutes, then add the chicken broth and the milk gradually, whisking, and cook until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt, black pepper, and the curry powder. It is a small amount and it is what separates this from every other cream sauce.
Off the heat, melt in most of the shredded cheese, then fold in the squeezed spinach and the diced turkey breast.
Pour the sauce over the rice, top with the remaining cheese, and bake at 375F for 30 minutes until bubbling and browned, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Huevos Rancheros Rice Bowls
ingredients: Seasoned Black Beans (Great Value): 1.6 cans (401 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 3 oz (88 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice and hold it warm. It is the base of every bowl, so make sure it is seasoned with salt while it cooks rather than after.
Cut the corn tortillas into strips and crisp them in a little vegetable oil until golden, then drain them on paper towels and salt them right away.
Warm the chopped turkey breast in a skillet with a splash of the salsa and a pinch of salt and black pepper, just until it is heated through.
Warm the drained black beans in a small pot with a little water so they stay loose rather than drying out in the fridge.
Fry the eggs in batches to your preference. For meal prep, cook them a shade past runny, because a broken yolk in a container on Thursday helps nobody.
Build the bowls: rice on the bottom, then beans, then turkey, then salsa spooned across the top.
Set an egg on each bowl, scatter the Mexican cheese blend and the chopped cilantro over it, and add the crisped tortilla strips last so they stay crunchy.

name: Turkey Kabsa Rice Bowls
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Toast the almonds dry in a skillet until they smell nutty, about 4 minutes, then set them aside with the golden raisins. This is your topping and it should not go in the pot.
Cut the turkey breast into large chunks. Heat the olive oil in a wide heavy pot and brown the turkey on all sides, then set it aside.
Cook the diced onion in the same pot for 6 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger, and the whole spice mix of cinnamon, cumin, coriander, allspice, paprika, cloves, and bay leaves, stirring one minute.

Stir in the tomato paste, then the diced tomatoes, grated carrot, and chopped jalapeno. Add the chicken broth, return the turkey, and simmer covered for 30 minutes until the turkey reaches 165F and the broth tastes like the dish.
Pull the turkey out and shred or chop it. Rinse the rice, then stir it into the simmering broth, cover, and cook on low 18 to 20 minutes until the liquid is gone and the grains are tender.
Fold the turkey back in with the butter and the lime juice, then let the pot rest covered for 10 minutes so the rice finishes steaming.
Move everything into your weighed pot and fluff it with a fork before you portion.

name: Turkey Keema Curry with Peas
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice per the package and set it aside.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large pot over medium and cook the onions until golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and jalapeno and cook 2 minutes more.
Add the ground cumin, turmeric, and coriander and toast in the aromatics for 30 seconds.
Add the ground turkey and brown it, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains and it reaches 165F.
Pour in the chicken broth and simmer 10 to 15 minutes until the gravy thickens and coats the meat.
Stir in the frozen peas and cook 3 minutes, then finish with the lemon juice and most of the cilantro.
Serve the keema over the rice with the remaining cilantro on top.

name: Turkey Kofta Bowls with Tahini Sauce
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mix the ground turkey with the minced garlic (save a third of it for the sauce), grated onion, chopped mint, cilantro, eggs, bread crumbs, and the spice blend of cumin, oregano, cinnamon, allspice, cloves, salt, black pepper, and red pepper flakes. Mix just until it comes together.
Shape the mixture into oval kofta, about 3 per serving. Wet hands make this far less annoying.
Bake at 400F for 18 to 20 minutes, or sear in a hot pan, until browned and 165F in the center.

Make the tahini sauce: whisk the tahini with the lemon juice, the reserved garlic, a big pinch of salt, and enough cold water to reach a pourable, creamy consistency. It will seize up first, keep whisking, it comes back.
Build bowls with the kofta and a generous spoon of tahini sauce over the top.
Store extra sauce in a separate container if you like it fresh, it also holds up fine mixed in.

name: Turkey Lasagna Soup
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.75 tbsp (4 g)
Diced Tomatoes & Green Chilies (Great Value (Ro-Tel style)): 2 cans (570 g)
Ziti Pasta (Great Value): 29 oz dry (820 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Heat a little olive oil in a big pot and brown the ground turkey hard, breaking it up, until it is cooked through to 165F. Let it get some color, because color is flavor in a soup that cooks this fast.
Add the diced onion and minced garlic and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the italian seasoning, dried basil, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper and toast them for one minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, the diced tomatoes with green chilies, and the beef broth, and simmer 20 minutes so it stops tasting like separate ingredients.
Cook the ziti separately in salted water and drain it. Keep it separate. Pasta cooked in soup keeps swelling in the fridge and by Wednesday you have a casserole.
Stir most of the parmesan into the hot soup and let it melt in, then tear the fresh basil over the pot off the heat.
Move the drained pasta into your weighed pot and hold the ricotta out for the containers.

name: Turkey Mac and Cheese Bake
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 16.75 oz dry (472 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 21 oz (593 g)
Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 21 oz (593 g)
Stuffing Mix (Kraft Stove Top (USDA SR)): 5.25 cups (289 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the pasta shells in heavily salted water two minutes short of the box time, then drain. They finish in the oven and mushy mac is unforgivable.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat, whisk in the flour, and cook two minutes until it smells toasted rather than raw.
Add the milk in stages, whisking constantly, and cook 5 to 7 minutes until the sauce is thick enough that a spoon drawn through it leaves a track.
Season with salt, black pepper, Italian seasoning, and a small pinch of nutmeg, which is the trick that makes cheese sauce taste like cheese sauce.
Pull the pot off the heat and melt in the shredded cheddar and the Mexican cheese blend a handful at a time. Direct heat will break a cheese sauce every time.
Fold in the diced turkey breast and the drained shells, then spread everything into a greased 9x13 pan.
Crush the stuffing mix over the top and bake at 350F for 25 to 30 minutes until the crust is golden and the sides bubble, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.

name: Turkey Manicotti with Ricotta
ingredients: Pasta Shells - jumbo (Great Value): 19.5 oz dry (552 g)
Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 18.75 oz (529 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the jumbo shells to just under done, about 2 minutes short of the box, then drain and spread them out so they do not stick together while you work.

Heat the olive oil, cook the diced onion 5 minutes, add the garlic for a minute, then brown the ground turkey until it is cooked through to 165F. Season with the italian seasoning, salt, and pepper and let it cool a few minutes.
Mix the ricotta with the chopped fresh basil and about a third of the mozzarella, then fold in the cooled turkey. Cool matters, because hot meat turns ricotta runny.
Spread a layer of marinara across the bottom of your baking pans so nothing sticks.
Stuff each shell with the filling using a spoon or a zip bag with the corner cut off, then set them in the pans in rows.
Cover with the rest of the marinara and the remaining mozzarella, then bake covered at 375F for 30 minutes, uncover, and bake 10 more until the top browns.
Rest 15 minutes, cook the rice, and move the rice into your weighed pot.

name: Turkey Maqluba (Upside-Down Rice Bake)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Slice the eggplant into rounds about half an inch thick, salt them on both sides, and let them drain in a colander for 30 minutes, then pat them dry.
Roast the eggplant slices on oiled sheet pans at 425F for 25 minutes, flipping once, until they are deeply browned and collapsed.
Brown the ground turkey in a large pot, then add the diced onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Stir in the tomato paste and the ground allspice, along with salt and black pepper, and cook two minutes until the paste darkens against the pot.
Add the canned diced tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes until the mixture thickens and the liquid mostly cooks off.
Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, then layer it into a large buttered baking dish: half the rice, the turkey mixture, the roasted eggplant, then the rest of the rice.
Pour the hot chicken broth over the top, cover tightly with foil, and bake at 375F for 45 minutes, then rest 15 minutes covered before fluffing and portioning.

name: Turkey Meatball Italian Wedding Soup
ingredients: Pasta Shells (Great Value): 18.75 oz dry (532 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Mix the ground turkey with the bread crumbs, eggs, milk, some of the grated parmesan and the chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and pepper, then roll the mix into small meatballs about the size of a grape.
Line a sheet pan, spread the meatballs out, and bake at 400F until browned, roughly 15 minutes. They finish cooking in the broth later, so do not fuss over the centers.
Chop the onion, carrots and celery small and sweat them in olive oil in your big pot over medium heat until soft, about 8 minutes.
Pour in the chicken broth, bring it to a simmer, then add the pasta shells and cook until they are just shy of tender.
Stir in the kale and the thawed chopped spinach and simmer until the greens go dark and silky.
Slide the meatballs into the pot, simmer a few minutes more so the flavors marry, then kill the heat and stir in the rest of the parmesan.

name: Turkey Meatball Marinara Pasta
ingredients: Mozzarella Cheese: 3 oz cubed + 3/4 cup shredded (510 g)
Black Pepper (Great Value): to taste (4 g)
steps: Brown 6.9 pounds of 93/7 ground turkey with the chopped onion and a splash of olive oil, breaking it into meatball-sized chunks.
Boil the penne separately until just tender, then drain.
Pour the marinara over the turkey and let it simmer so the sauce soaks in.
Toss the cooked pasta into the sauce until everything is coated.
Finish each container with a shower of parmesan while it is still hot.

name: Turkey Meatball Sub Bake
ingredients: Reduced Fat Mozzarella (Great Value): 16.75 oz (476 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Chop the smoked turkey sausage fine, or run it through a food processor, and mix it with the ground turkey, the eggs, the bread crumbs, the parmesan, minced garlic, minced onion, chopped mushrooms, salt, and black pepper.
Roll the mixture into meatballs and set them on lined sheet pans. Two per serving is the target size, so aim a little bigger than a golf ball.
Bake at 400F for 20 minutes until browned and cooked through to 165F.
Warm the marinara in a pot, then slide the baked meatballs in and simmer them 15 minutes so they drink up the sauce instead of just wearing it.
Cook the rice and move it into your weighed pot.
Split the buns and lay them out. Do not assemble them all now, since bread that sits in sauce for four days is a texture nobody wants.
Shred or portion out the mozzarella and keep it in its own small container.

name: Turkey Meatloaf with Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 7 oz (198 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.

Melt the butter in a skillet and cook the diced onion and green bell pepper for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for one minute and let the mixture cool. Hot vegetables will start cooking the egg.
In a large bowl, whisk the eggs with the heavy cream, Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, salt, and black pepper, then stir in the bread crumbs and let them soak for 5 minutes.
Add the ground turkey, the cooled vegetables, and the shredded cheddar. Mix with your hands only until it comes together. Overworking meatloaf turns it dense and rubbery.
Divide the mixture between three loaf pans or shape it into three free-form loaves on a sheet pan. Smaller loaves cook faster and slice more evenly than one giant brick.
Stir the ketchup and barbecue sauce together and brush half of it over the loaves, then bake at 350F for 45 to 55 minutes until the centers read 165F.
Brush on the rest of the glaze and return the loaves for 10 minutes so it sets into a lacquer instead of running off.
Cook the rice while the loaves rest at least 15 minutes, then slice the meatloaf and portion it over the rice.

name: Turkey Migas Skillet
ingredients: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 9.5 oz (267 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cut the corn tortillas into strips and fry them in the vegetable oil in batches over medium-high until they are crisp and lightly browned, then drain them on paper towels.
Pour off most of the oil, then brown the ground turkey in the same skillet, breaking it into crumbles and seasoning it with salt and black pepper.
Add the diced onion, red bell pepper, and jalapeno and cook 6 minutes until they soften, then stir in the drained diced tomatoes and cook off the excess liquid.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt until the yolks and whites are fully combined, with no streaks left.
Drop the heat to medium-low and pour the eggs into the skillet. Push them slowly across the pan with a spatula rather than stirring fast; you want soft folds, not curds.
When the eggs are about three quarters set, fold in the fried tortilla strips so they soften slightly but keep some crunch.
Kill the heat, scatter the Mexican cheese blend over the top, and cover for two minutes to melt it before portioning.

name: Turkey Minestrone
ingredients: Red Pepper Flakes (Great Value): 0.25 tbsp (1 g)
Pasta Shells (Great Value): 39 oz dry (1103 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Dice the onion, carrot, and celery small and cook them in the olive oil in a big pot for 10 minutes until soft and sweet. This is the base of the soup and rushing it is the most common mistake.
Add the minced garlic, the oregano, dried basil, red pepper flakes, salt, and black pepper, and cook one minute.
Cut the turkey breast into small cubes, add them to the pot, and cook until they are no longer pink and reach 165F.
Add the crushed tomatoes and the chicken broth and simmer 20 minutes so the flavors come together.
Add the diced zucchini and the drained cannellini beans and simmer 10 minutes more, until the zucchini is tender but not falling apart.
Stir in the chopped kale for the last 3 minutes and taste for salt one more time.
Cook the pasta shells separately, drain them, and move them into your weighed pot.

name: Turkey Nasi Goreng
ingredients: Sweet Soy Sauce (ABC (Kecap Manis)): 6 oz (168 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice a day ahead if you can and chill it uncovered. Cold rice is the entire secret to fried rice that is not mush.
Cut the turkey breast into small cubes and season them with salt and black pepper.
Heat some of the vegetable oil in your largest skillet or wok over high heat and sear the turkey in batches until browned and cooked through to 165F. Set it aside.
Add the rest of the oil, then the sliced onion, minced garlic, and chopped jalapeno, and stir-fry 3 minutes until fragrant and just softening.
Add the cold rice and press it into the pan, letting it sit undisturbed for a minute at a time so it toasts, then tossing. Do this for about 5 minutes.
Pour in the sweet soy sauce, return the turkey, and toss for 2 minutes until every grain is dark and coated. Taste for salt.
Fry the eggs separately, one per container, and slice the cucumber into rounds while the rice cools enough to portion.

name: Turkey Noodle Casserole
ingredients: Egg Noodles (Great Value wide): 20 oz dry (564 g)
Sweet Whole Kernel Corn (Great Value): 1.2 cans (520 g)
Cheddar Cheese, Shredded (Great Value): 25 oz (712 g)
steps: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Boil the egg noodles in salted water two minutes short of the package time and drain them. They will keep cooking in the sauce, and overcooked noodles turn to paste in a bake.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat, add the garlic for one minute, then whisk in the flour and cook it for two minutes.
Pour in the milk slowly while whisking, then cook 4 to 5 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to coat a spoon.
Season with the dried thyme, Italian seasoning, salt, and black pepper, then melt in about three quarters of the shredded cheddar off the heat so it does not go grainy.
Fold in the diced turkey breast, the frozen peas, the drained corn, and the cooked noodles until everything is coated.
Spread it into a greased 9x13 pan, scatter the rest of the cheddar over the top, and bake at 350F for 25 to 30 minutes until bubbling and browned in spots.
Rest 10 minutes before portioning so the sauce sets around the noodles instead of running out of them.
